Key concepts
Stakeholder engagement and materiality
We recognise that stakeholder engagement is crucial 
for accelerating corporate change and innovation. 
Our material priorities are derived directly from 
stakeholder input that helps us in driving transformation 
and innovation.ESG commitments
At UPL, long-term sustainability is central to our vision, 
anchored by robust and consistent ESG performance. 
Our ESG initiatives are regularly reviewed by the Board, 
with the Sustainability Committee overseeing strategy 
execution and guiding management. Having secured the 
global #1 rank by DJSI for consecutive years, our ambitious 
2030 targets remain on track. Building on our 2025 
achievements, we remain committed to driving meaningful 
sustainability outcomes through future-ready practices.

=== page 4 ===
UPL achieved a landmark performance in FY26, 
delivering exceptional financial performance and 
solidifying its leadership across global agricultural 
markets. This transformative success follows a 
challenging macro-period marked by turbulent 
global commodity prices and widespread farm 
economics stress, serving as a defining turnaround 
year that showcased our structural resilience and 
ability to accelerate profitable growth. Navigating 
through those past external sector headwinds, 
we successfully pivoted by establishing and 
scaling our pure-play business platforms. Backed 
by strategic clarity and disciplined execution, 
this high-impact model allowed us to maximise 
market opportunities, delivering a strong 11% 
increase in consolidated revenue to ₹51,839 crore, 
fuelled by an overall 8% volume-led growth across 
major markets.Our focus on high-value innovation and 
continuous product differentiation across 
our specialised platforms has further 
de-risked the business from legacy 
commodity price volatility. This structural 
shift is clearly demonstrated by a robust 
220 bps expansion in contribution margins 
to 41.2% alongside an 18% surge in 
EBITDA to ₹9,588 crore, driven by optimal 
plant utilisation capacities and strict cost 
control. Underpinning this operational 
recovery is a relentless commitment to 
absolute financial discipline. Our efficient 
working capital cycles and enhanced risk 
management frameworks helped generate 
an operationally resilient free cash flow 
to equity (adjusted for change in working 
capital) of ₹4,450 crore, reflecting our 
highly optimised cash conversion cycle.
Crucially, proactive debt management and 
aggressive deleveraging remained at the 
centre of our capital strategy. We repaid 
debt obligation of $500 million in March 
through robust internal cash accruals that 
aided our strong debt reduction through 
the year, reducing our net debt-to-EBITDA 
gearing to 1.6x.

Financial highlights
FY26 marked a period of accelerated growth, characterised by volume-led 
expansion across international crop protection, seeds and post-harvest 
treatment, and specialty chemistries markets. Strategic new product 
introductions enhanced the portfolio, improved resistance management and 
sustained strong operational momentum. Margins expanded significantly, 
driven by new launches, optimised capacity utilisation, lower raw material 
costs and manufacturing excellence. Sharp operational discipline and 
strong internal accruals resulted in robust free cash flows, while aggressive 
deleveraging initiatives and successful refinancing strategies led to a 
substantial reduction in debt, significantly strengthening the balance sheet.

UPL at a glance
For more than fifty years, UPL has 
pioneered high-impact agri-solutions 
globally, consistently navigating 
through complex market cycles 
and expanding across geographical 
boundaries with deep operational 
resilience. In today’s evolving 
operating landscape, we remain 
deeply focused on our mission to 
develop sustainable food systems.UPL operates through highly agile, pure-play platforms 
spanning advanced seeds and post-harvest treatments, 
conventional crop protection, BioSolutions, specialty 
chemistries and high-tech agronomic services. These 
solutions are strategically engineered to boost farmer 
productivity, adapt to climate shifts and maximise 
long-term grower profitability through innovative, 
tailored approaches.
We are transforming global food chains, empowering 
growers and advancing sustainable farming practices. 
Backed by our robust manufacturing footprint and 
centralised Global Capability Centres (GCCs), we offer a 
powerful mix of patented and post-patent agricultural 
solutions that support every stage of the crop lifecycle. 
Driven by our landmark global #AFarmerCan campaign, 
our ambition is to make every food product more 
sustainable, enriching farming communities, protecting 
regional ecosystems and strengthening the global food 
supply chain.Our Vision is to be a global icon for 
technology growth and innovation
Our Mission is to change the game, 
to make every single food product 
more sustainable.
Global reach and strong 
distribution network
As a top-five global agrochemical 
player, our footprint spans over 140 
countries. Approximately, 66% of 
revenue is generated from Latin 
America, Europe and North America, 
insulating our business from 
localised market cycles and weather 
disruptions. Complemented by 
market leadership in India, this 
extensive international penetration 
gives us an unparalleled distribution 
network to roll out new solutions 
rapidly at scale.Backward integrated 
manufacturing excellence 
Our operational resilience is anchored 
by an end-to-end backward integrated 
manufacturing ecosystem. Spanning 
across 43 state-of-the-art global 
facilities, this footprint optimises 
asset utilisation, ensuring supply 
assurance and maintaining proximity 
to our customers while also mitigating 
input cost volatility. This scale 
directly underpins our healthy long-
term margin resilience and robust 
operating profitability.Focus on innovation  
led growth
Innovation drives our long-term 
value creation across the crop 
lifecycle, spanning seeds, seed 
treatments, crop protection 
and post-harvest preservation 
treatment. Our deep-tech R&D 
pipeline forms a defensive moat, 
with ~30% of our agchem portfolio 
being IP protected. This helps 
capture premium market segments,  
driving high-margin farmgate 
adoption globally.KEY STRENGTHS

=== page 10 ===
Profitable 
growth  powered  
by operational excellence 
and financial discipline
UPL's FY26 performance demonstrates that long-term 
profitability is built on disciplined execution, financial resilience 
and a relentless focus on business quality. As the global 
agricultural sector navigated geopolitical uncertainty, evolving 
trade dynamics and fluctuating farmer economics, we remained 
focused on what we could control - strengthening margins, 
enhancing cash generation and improving capital efficiency.
The result was a year of broad-based profitable growth. 
Revenue increased by 11%, EBITDA grew by 18% and PATMI 
more than doubled, reflecting the benefits of volume-led 
growth, market share gains and improved commercial execution 
across key geographies. Importantly, this performance 
was accompanied by contribution margin expansion across 
platforms, highlighting the increasing quality of earnings and 
the effectiveness of portfolio optimisation initiatives.
Strong operating performance translated 
into robust cash generation, enabling UPL 
to accelerate its deleveraging journey. Gross 
debt reduced by $850 million, while net debt 
declined by over $400 million during the 
year.* Consequently, Net Debt-to-EBITDA 
improved to around 1.6x, reinforcing 
financial flexibility and strengthening the 
balance sheet. Importantly, our diversified 
business portfolio spanning crop protection, 
seeds and post-harvest and specialty 
chemicals further strengthened financial 
resilience by reducing concentration risk 
and creating multiple growth and cash 
generation engines across market cycles. 
As we continue to scale our growth 
platforms, Advanta expanded its global seed 
franchise while SUPERFORM strengthened 
its presence in specialty chemicals. Together, 
these businesses are creating diversified 
avenues of growth, enabling us to convert 
operational momentum into long-term 
shareholder value.

needs of growers worldwide. Our product range includes advanced seeds 
and post-harvest treatment, crop protection, BioSolutions and specialty 
chemistries, all supported by our expert agronomic services. Through our 
platforms, we are accelerating our market growth, focusing on product 
innovation and capturing better margins across the entire agricultural 
supply chain.

UPL Corporation Ltd.
Our international pure-play crop protection platform, UPL Corporation Ltd. (UPL Corp), delivers integrated crop protection 
and biological solutions driven by a sustainable, farmer-first approach. Guided by our OpenAg® model, we foster cross-
industry collaboration to co-develop locally relevant, scalable innovations. Through platforms like ProNutiva®, we 
combine conventional chemistry with our Natural Plant Protection (NPP) portfolio to enhance plant health and resilience 
throughout the crop lifecycle.
Farmer resilience is central to our mission. Our 'closer to farmer' go-to-market model provides world-class agronomic 
solutions and hands-on support to help growers navigate climatic and economic volatility while boosting productivity and 
profitability. Backed by this robust execution, UPL Corp achieved strong volume-driven performance in FY26, delivering 
an 11% top-line revenue expansion.
“Our international crop protection business 
delivered a strong growth across key regions and 
segments in FY26. Driven by exceptional operational 
excellence, superior product value delivery and a 
strong internal culture.  
I am also pleased to share that despite a challenging 
macro market, we have delivered six consecutive 
quarters of EBITDA growth, with continued focus on 
expanding our market share.
Further, our focus on improving efficiency and 
profitability throughout the year enabled us to 
significantly expand our contribution and EBITDA 
margins. As we look to the future, our commitment 
to continuous innovation is not just about 
maintaining our market leadership, it is about 
empowering growers worldwide and shaping a more 
resilient, sustainable future for global agriculture.”
Mike Frank
CEO, UPL Corporation Ltd.

Quality
We enforce strict quality control matrices across all stages of our product lifecycle, cementing our reputation 
as an industry benchmark. Our commitment to operational excellence is driven by a comprehensive quality 
management framework that combines proactive interventions with systematic site audits, safeguarding 
performance at every milestone. Maintaining close, direct touchpoints with growers and channel partners 
provides the real-world feedback necessary to continuously optimise and upgrade our formulations, ensuring 
they consistently align with evolving field conditions.

Smart demand forecasting
Our AI-powered forecasting engine delivers materially 
higher accuracy than traditional manual methods by 
learning from large volumes of historical, market and 
seasonal data to detect demand patterns that conventional 
approaches miss. This sharper forecasting aligns 
production schedules with dynamic global market demand, 
enabling more efficient inventory management and agile, 
data-driven supply chain decisions. By reducing excess 
stock and minimising stock-outs, these capabilities 
optimise working capital, freeing up cash and 
strengthening the resilience of our operations.
Democratising AI and data-led decision making
Through our secure enterprise AI platform, we are 
enabling scalable access to advanced AI tools across 
the organisation. Combined with self-service analytics

Together, these initiatives reflect UPL’s commitment 
to building a digitally empowered, agile and future-

UPL SAS
UPL Sustainable Agri Solutions Limited (UPL SAS) continues to 
revolutionise the Indian agricultural landscape and fortify grower 
livelihoods, unlocking exceptional EBITDA growth in FY26 amidst 
volatile monsoon cycles. UPL SAS prioritises advancing climate-smart 
cultivation and deploys high-value, localised technologies engineered 
specifically for the diverse needs of India's rural markets. Through the 
next-generation agronomic tools, it enables cultivators to optimise 
farmgate productivity, minimise resource degradation and secure 
enduring financial sustainability.
We are engineering end-to-end integrated solutions that drive value across the agricultural value chain, combining 
products, direct-to-retail digital commerce, on-demand spray and mechanisation services, water conservation and 
carbon sequestration in agricultural systems. Our strategy is to create and scale differentiated brands across crops, thus 
diversifying our revenue base and improving competitive advantage and profitability.
Leading
Crop protection company  
in India
“FY26 was a year of continuity and transformation 
for UPL SAS. We continued our relentless focus on 
business quality, inventory, receivables and price 
discipline, which allowed us to expand profitability 
and strengthen our balance sheet. By scaling new 
differentiated products effectively, we overcame 
weather headwinds and generic pressures to preserve 
revenue. Despite industry-wide price erosion, a 
challenging monsoon and planned phase-out of older 
molecules, we successfully expanded our contribution 
and EBITDA margins.Structurally, we have realigned our sales incentives 
to reflect our strategy of disciplined yet aspirational 
growth, embedding advanced AI and Machine Learning 
models to predict credit default risk and optimising 
forecasting. As we scale up our elite brands and 
activate our 'Launch Big and Scale Fast' strategy across 
fresh crop segments like corn and sugarcane, we are 
utilising digital tools to drive alignment."
Ravishankar Cherukuri
CEO, UPL SAS

nurture.farm
The nurture.farm platform supports over 2.5 
million farmers across India, empowering 
them with localised digital tools, effectively 
breaking accessibility barriers for smallholder 
communities. Through its user-friendly mobile 
framework, the platform offers a seamless 
combination of high-impact farm mechanisation, 
predictive diagnostics and precise field services

input costs and simplify access to essential 
resources. The nurture.farm services are also a 
competitive advantage in our scale-up brands.nurture.farm retail 
The nurture.farm retail platform is India’s premier 
B2B agri-input marketplace, optimising the 
rural supply chain by directly connecting agri-
retailers with leading manufacturers. Through 
a sophisticated digital ecosystem, it removes 
logistical friction to provide on-demand visibility 
into a verified portfolio of crop protection, 
nutrition and biological solutions. Backed by 
integrated fintech capabilities, it delivers flexible 
credit solutions, secure inventory financing and 
digital safeguards that protect rural businesses 
against counterfeit products.

UPL SAS crop protection – business  
performance review
Transformed to drive sustainable growth
During FY26, we fundamentally transformed our 
operations to drive sustainable, resilient growth across 
the Indian market. Our business elevated its operational 
quality, defending and expanding profit margins through 
a highly disciplined approach to pricing and strategic 
improvements in the product mix. Concurrently, a rigorous 
emphasis on capital health optimised working capital 
cycles. This was achieved through prudent credit controls, 
strict inventory management and restructuring sales 
incentives to align directly with cash collection.
The portfolio's overall quality and market depth also 
experienced robust advancement throughout the fiscal 
year. We achieved significant expansion into new crop 
segments, specifically scaling our footprint across highly 
lucrative corn and sugarcane acreages. This portfolio diversification was further amplified by exceptional 
execution in product launches and rapid commercial scale-
ups. To ensure long-term pipeline resilience and technical 
superiority, our platform actively secured and leveraged 
strategic R&D partnerships, systematically strengthening 
its high-value crop protection offerings.
Driving this commercial engine was a deep commitment 
to digital transformation across both retail networks 
and field operations. Our proprietary 'Farmily' retailer 
loyalty programme witnessed high engagement and 
strong reward redemption rates, cementing closer 
relationships with local channel partners. Internally, the 
high adoption of the 'Swift Squad' digital platform brought 
unprecedented real-time visibility to ground-level field 
activities. By embedding advanced analytics and Machine 
Learning (ML) models into our core governance, we 
successfully automated default prediction and precision 
customer profiling, turning data intelligence into a strong 
competitive advantage.

The value 
curve
FY26 marked a transformational milestone 
in our evolution with the announcement 
of a strategic group reorganisation 
designed to simplify the corporate 
structure, sharpen business focus and 
unlock long-term shareholder value. Built 
around three distinct platforms - UPL 
Global SAS (crop protection), Advanta 
(seeds and post-harvest treatment) and 
SUPERFORM (specialty chemicals), the 
new structure positions each business to 
pursue its growth ambitions with greater 
agility, dedicated capital structures and 
independent governance.
The proposed reorganisation reflects our 
belief that the intrinsic value of our diverse 
businesses can be better recognised 
through focused platforms rather than 
within a consolidated structure. By 
creating pure-play entities with clear 
strategic mandates, we aim to improve 
transparency, enhance capital allocation 
and enable more effective benchmarking 
against global peers.SPOTLIGHT
The entire composite scheme of arrangement 
is cash-neutral and tax-neutral, ensuring that 
there is no dilution of minority shareholder 
rights or change to the cumulative debt profile 
at the consolidated group level. Furthermore, 
UPL Limited will remain an active operating 
company, maintaining a key revenue engine of 
over ₹10,000 crore post-reorganisation through 
the full consolidation of SUPERFORM and the 
continuation of formulation supply contracts, 
while acting as the group’s central incubation 
arm for scaling adjacent businesses.
Importantly, the new structure will preserve 
the strengths of our ecosystem. Shared 
manufacturing capabilities, R&D expertise, 
treasury functions and digital infrastructure 
will continue to provide scalable benefits and 
operational synergies while independent 
leadership teams drive platform-specific 
growth strategies.
Alongside simplifying the structure, the 
reorganisation will support our ongoing capital 
optimisation and value creation agenda. With 
stronger governance, improved financial visibility 
and multiple pathways for future value discovery, 
the new model creates a powerful foundation for 
sustainable growth and enhanced shareholder 
returns over the long term.Proposed structure

Seeds and 
post-harvest
High-yielding seeds are a vital investment for farmers, 
as their quality directly influences yield. We stand at the 
forefront of delivering advanced, high-quality seeds 
worldwide, tailored to local conditions through a focus 
on research and innovation. We support sustainable 
farming and farmer profitability by leveraging our 
expertise in biotechnology and research to create climate-
smart seeds with robust yields. Our leadership in FY26 
was underscored by exceptional germplasm, advanced 
technological know-how and a dedicated global team 
that drove an outstanding 23% revenue growth, offering 
cutting-edge solutions that elevate productivity across 
diverse geographies.Advanta
Our group company, Advanta, stands as a key player within 
the UPL Group, managing both Indian and international 
seed businesses and has established itself as a global 
seeds platform for high-value crops. In September 2025, 
we acquired DECCO, the post-harvest treatment business. 
This acquisition represents a strategic expansion beyond 
our seed business into the adjacent post-harvest segment. 
It has enabled us to expand and strengthen our presence 
in the broader agricultural value chain, whilst enhancing 
business complementarity and diversifying our revenues 
by adding a stable, service-led post-harvest business to 
our global seeds business. Together, Advanta and DECCO 
connect the journey,  ensuring food reaches people fresher 
and with greater value.
"We are building a globally competitive, science-led 
seeds and post-harvest platform. FY26 was a year of 
strong execution, delivering 23% revenue growth and 
30% EBITDA growth, led by the continued momentum 
of all our key crops like field corn, fresh corn, sunflower, 
canola etc. Our focus remains on disciplined growth, 
resilient profitability and long-term value creation. 
During the year, we successfully integrated our post-
harvest business, strengthening our ability to offer 
end-to-end solutions to farmers. Anchored in our 
'Farmer First' philosophy, we combine deep market 
engagement with a strong innovation engine to develop climate-resilient, high-performance solutions. 
Our diversified geographic and product portfolio 
helps mitigate climate volatility while positioning us 
to benefit from structural demand growth in food, 
feed and biofuels. With a differentiated pipeline and 
expanding market presence, we remain committed to 
creating sustainable value for farmers, customers and 
shareholders." 
Bhupen Dubey
CEO, Advanta

Innovation and smart R&D

Comprehensive product

The commercial portfolio has 
grown to over 900 hybrid varieties, 
with a clear roadmap to surpass 
1,000 hybrids across 40 crops. 
The product mix is primarily led by 
field corn at 40% of total revenue,

crops at 15% and vegetables/fresh 
corn at 10%.Global footprint and market 
penetration
Operating across the Americas,

deployment of traits.

Strategy
We have accelerated a range of strategic initiatives for the

each milestone achieved reinforces our commitment to 
delivering superior solutions and robust performance. 
Backed by optimised asset utilisation and strong operational 
discipline, these initiatives continue to drive sustainable 
margin expansion and long-term value creation.
Accelerating innovation
We have prioritised the registration of new active 
ingredients (AIs) and structurally enhanced our 
innovation rate, driving a powerful surge in new 
product launches across global markets. This dynamic 
approach ensures our pipeline remains robust, resilient 
against pest resistance and highly responsive to 
evolving agricultural needs. Backed by advanced R&D 
and accelerated market approvals, these high-value 
introductions have successfully fortified our portfolio, 
delivering cutting-edge solutions that sustain long-term 
growth and maximise value for growers worldwide.Sustaining profitable growth
Our focus on high-margin product mix, aggressive 
product level SKU rationalisation, portfolio and the 
global implementation of rigorous channel 'sellout' 
strategies has structurally sustained our profitability. 
We have accelerated regulatory clearances to swiftly 
bring differentiated, resistance-breaking formulations 
to market. Backed by optimised manufacturing capacity

disciplined working capital management, these 
initiatives continue to drive robust operating cash 
flows and long-term margin expansion across our 
business segments.Driving operational excellence and

We have institutionalised rigorous financial discipline 
globally by optimising our working capital cycle, 
shrinking cash conversion timelines and enforcing 
stringent credit risk management policies. These 
efforts are paired with targeted, productivity-driven

cleansing our commercial portfolio of dilutive, low-

structural, long-term margin expansion. Elevating ESG and sustainability

globally, reinforcing our core commitment to sustainable

driving awareness around regenerative practices. We

farmers and retailers through comprehensive health 
and safety drives, localised insurance initiatives and 
sustainable crop-management practices that secure 
long-term food security and community well-being.
Pioneering digital transformation

alongside an expanding vegetable seeds portfolio 
across strategic growth hubs in India and Australia.

Risk management
To navigate a dynamic business environment, we manage risk through a 
Group-wide Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework that enables 
early identification, minimises downside exposure and directly supports 
our strategic objectives. Benchmarked against leading global standards 
such as ISO 31000:2018 and the COSO ERM Framework, this structured 
approach embeds risk-informed thinking into strategy, capital allocation and 
performance management. 
This year, we strengthened our resilience by introducing 
the Integrated Risk Assessment Framework (IRAF) 
alongside an in-house digital risk management tool, 
establishing a data-driven risk culture that delivers 
near-real-time visibility and reporting across all levels of 
the organisation.
Risk governance
We manage risk through a Group-wide Enterprise Risk 
Management (ERM) framework, underpinned by a clear 
governance structure that defines who owns, oversees and 
assures risk across the organisation. 
Oversight cascades from the top of the organisation. The 
Board of Directors bears ultimate responsibility for risk Risk management framework
The framework provides a consistent, structured approach 
to managing risk across every entity, geography and 
business line, embedding risk-informed thinking into 
strategy, capital allocation and performance management. 
The framework is benchmarked against leading 
international standards such as ISO 31000:2018 and the 
COSO ERM Framework. It operates within the governance 
structure described above, with the Board, the Risk 
Management Committee and the Centralised Risk Office 
providing oversight, ownership and assurance.
Strengthening our framework this year: The 
Integrated Risk Assessment Framework (IRAF)
During the year, we embarked on a journey to strengthen 
this framework by introducing an Integrated Risk 
Assessment Framework (IRAF) that sharpens the way 
risks are assessed and prioritised, anchored in our 
business objectives.
In this, risks are organised into a structured category, 
viz., Strategic, Operational, Financial, Compliance and 
Technology. Each risk will then be assessed on a likelihood-
and-impact matrix and further defined against financial 
and non-financial criteria. Risks will then be tiered into 
High, Medium and Low categories (Tier 1/2/3) to focus 
management attention and resource allocation where it 
matters most. 
These risks will be further benchmarked against leading 
global references such as Allianz Risk Barometer, Aon 
Global Risk Management Survey, WEF Global Risks Report, 
etc., to corroborate completeness and capture existing and 
emerging risks.
Digital risk management
To operationalise the IRAF, we have developed an in-
house digital risk management tool that delivers risk 
insights across various levels of the organisation through 
interactive dashboards, heat maps and trend analysis, 
enabling near-real-time visibility and reporting. Rollout has 
commenced, advancing us towards a more resilient, data-
driven risk culture.management and for the effectiveness of the framework. 
The Risk Management Committee, constituted under 
Regulation 21 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, oversees 
implementation of the ERM framework and reviews the risk 
register, appetite utilisation and mitigation plans. 
Three lines of risk management
Accountability follows a three-line model: the first line, 
directly owns risk and embeds it into day-to-day activities. 
The second line, the Centralised Risk Office together 
with the other group level functions, sets frameworks, 
standards and provides oversight, and the third line, 
provides independent assurance to the Board and Audit 
Committee. This segregation ensures risk management is 
both embedded and independently assured.Within this governance and accountability structure, the Group operates a common risk management framework, 
described below.

Our Group’s Risk Appetite Statement is reviewed at least 
annually and currently has zero tolerance for compliance 
and regulatory breaches. Based on the pursuit of its 
strategic objectives, the Group makes a decision on risk 
appetite, keeping the risk-to-reward ratio in mind.  
These boundaries are translated into operational limits 
across businesses and functions and are supported by a 
defined escalation protocol, so that risk-taking remains 
deliberate, measured and within Board-approved limits.
Frequency of assessment
Because risks shift over time, risks are reviewed on a 
recurring cycle rather than as a point-in-time event. The 
Group risk function reviews and refreshes the risk register 
at least twice a year and more frequently as required, 
while the Risk Management Committee reviews it at 
least annually.Risk management process audit
As the third line of defence, Group Internal Audit provides 
independent assurance to the Board and its Committees 
over the design and operating effectiveness of the risk 
management framework. Operating independently of 
the first and second lines that own and manage risk, it 
evaluates whether risks are being managed and controls 
are operating effectively across the Group. Its findings 
inform the continuous improvement of the framework, 
complementing the periodic Risk and Control Self-
Assessments performed by the business.

Emerging Risks
Beyond the principal risks set out earlier, UPL also 
tracks emerging risks that are still developing but 
could become material over time. Two stand out for 
a sustainable Agri solutions company: the loss of 
biodiversity on which agriculture depends and the adverse 
outcomes that can arise as we scale digital and artificial 
intelligence technologies.
Biodiversity loss and ecosystem collapse
The global food system is a primary driver of biodiversity 
loss, with intensive agriculture among the leading threats 
to species extinction. This creates a negative feedback 
loop: degradation of ecosystems, soil health, pollinators 
and habitats reduces crop productivity and undermines 
the long-term resilience of agricultural systems.
As a result of this, declining productivity, increasing 
supply volatility and tightening environmental regulations 
may impact revenues and margins. In parallel, reduced 
farmer profitability may weaken demand for crop 
protection solutions.
To mitigate this, our ProNutiva® programme combines 
BioSolutions (biocontrol, biostimulants, soil health and 
innovative nutrition) with conventional crop protection to 
improve farming systems' climate resilience, emerging pest 
and disease resistance, soil health and fertility, water use 
and reduce residues, while protecting farmer economics 
and meeting evolving food-chain requirements. This transition is supported by clear portfolio and 
innovation targets: UPL Corp aims to reach 50% of 
revenues from sustainable and differentiated solutions by 
2030, with ~80% of its innovation pipeline aligned to these 
solutions, a target innovation rate of over 20% and strong 
growth ambitions for its BioSolutions division (NPP).
We further build ecosystem resilience through 
Regenerative and Sustainable Agriculture programmes 
covering over 100,000 hectares globally that combine 
sustainable farming practices with BioSolutions and carbon 
benefits. In parallel, we collaborate across the food value 
chain to scale sustainable farming systems, with projects 
covering directly and indirectly approximately 2.6 million 
hectares in 2025, helping align agricultural production with 
environment protection.Adverse outcomes of AI technologies
As UPL expands its focus on digital solutions, unintended 
AI outcomes could increasingly threaten the way 
we operate.
This technological risk arises where artificial intelligence 
models deployed across our business processes are 
incorrect, biased, or malfunctioning, producing flawed 
recommendations or unreliable automated decisions.
The potential impact is that such outputs may trigger 
operational errors, regulatory scrutiny and compliance 
failures, customer dissatisfaction and product-
performance concerns, raising remediation and 
regulatory costs.
To mitigate the adverse outcomes of artificial intelligence 
technologies, we distinctly label artificial intelligence-
generated content and artificial intelligence-driven 
decisions. We deploy mechanisms to detect and correct 
model drift or degradation over time and conduct regular 
fairness and bias assessments of deployed models. 
Humans are kept “in the loop” for critical decisions and data 
privacy is respected in the use and development of artificial 
intelligence. Clear accountability is assigned for artificial 
intelligence-driven outcomes and employees are trained 
on the ethical use and security of artificial intelligence. Risk management
58 Annual Report 2025-26 59 Annual Report 2025-26
Corporate overview Statutory Reports Sustainability Management speaks Notice Financial StatementsRisk management in product development
Integrated approach:  Risk management is embedded 
directly within our research and product development 
process, fostering an effective, organisation-wide risk 
culture built on shared accountability across functions. 
Potential risks are identified at an early stage, from 
molecule selection through process development and 
commercialisation, so that mitigation is built into a 
product’s design rather than addressed after launch. 
This proactive approach helps safeguard our innovation 
pipeline and the long-term sustainability of our portfolio.
Principal risks:  The Company continuously evaluates 
key risks, including potential delays in new-product 
development and launch, the evolving intellectual-property 
and patent landscape, generic and cost competition, 
regulatory changes and bans and broader sustainability 
and market-share pressures. Each is assessed for 
its likelihood and potential impact on our growth 
and competitiveness.
Mitigation:  Our approach rests on early assessment, 
backward integration to secure key inputs and disciplined 
portfolio prioritisation, reinforced by close cross-functional 
alignment among the R&D, intellectual-property, 
regulatory, supply-chain and commercial teams. Oversight 
of multiple projects and stakeholders across our R&D 
divisions keeps risk mitigation an integral and ongoing part 
of how products are developed and delivered.

The past three years have been among the most 
challenging for global crop protection industry. Post-
COVID destocking, falling active ingredient prices and 
changing channel dynamics tested the resilience of every 
participant. I am pleased to report that our business has 
emerged stronger and better positioned for future growth.
In FY26, we delivered strong revenue growth and 
significant margin improvement through innovation and 
organisational efficiency, reflecting the strategic decisions 
taken during the industry downturn and supported by our 
teams, channel partners and grower customers worldwide.
A cycle that tested and strengthened us
As China reopened following COVID-19 restrictions, excess 
industry capacity led to significant decline in product 
prices. Further, distributors worked through elevated 
inventory levels from prior supply shortages. The resulting 
correction lasted nearly 18 months, characterised by 
pricing pressure and sustained channel destocking.
By the end of 2024, market conditions began to 
stabilise, with further improvement in FY26. This created 
opportunities for companies with strong customer 
relationships, disciplined operations and competitive 
portfolios. At UPL, our focus remained on proactive 
execution rather than defensive positioning,  
a characteristic that continues to define our business.Delivering in a challenging environment
In FY26, we delivered 11% revenue growth, led by volumes 
across herbicides and fungicides. Contribution margins 
increased by more than 250 basis points to 35.1%, 
supported by a richer product mix, supply-chain discipline 
and improved capacity utilisation.
Over six consecutive quarters, we have delivered growth 
in revenue and EBITDA. This demonstrates disciplined 
working capital management, deeper customer connect, 
innovation and strong commercial execution.
Growth was broad-based across key regions. Herbicides 
such as clethodim and s-metolachlor performed strongly, 
while differentiated insecticide brands including Feroce®, 
Perito®, Propose® and Constel® gained traction. Our NPP 
business continued to grow across Europe and Asia Pacific, 
while post-patent portfolio delivered solid performance in 
North America, Asia Pacific and Brazil.
Innovation as a competitive advantage
Innovation remains central to our strategy and increasingly 
contributes to financial performance. During FY26, we 
launched over 300 new products globally, generating 
around $160 million in revenue. These products support 
our objective of mix-led margin expansion.

Message from the Group CFO
Dear Shareholders,
As I reflect on FY26, I am encouraged not only by the 
growth we delivered, but also by its quality. Stronger 
margins, higher cash generation, reduced leverage and a 
resilient balance sheet reflect the significant progress we 
made in strengthening UPL’s financial foundations.
The year was shaped by geopolitical uncertainty, evolving 
trade dynamics and continued pressure on grower 
economics. Despite these headwinds, demand remained 
stable across major agricultural markets. Supported by 
our diversified portfolio and global footprint, we delivered 
broad-based growth while enhancing business quality 
through disciplined portfolio management, prudent risk 
management and a focus on value-accretive opportunities.
As I complete my first full year as Group CFO, I am pleased 
to report meaningful progress across our key financial 
priorities: profitable growth, disciplined capital allocation, 
cash generation and balance sheet strength.
Growth with improved business quality
For us, business quality is measured by our ability to 
convert growth into higher profitability and stronger 
returns. FY26 delivered meaningful progress across 
these dimensions.
Revenue grew 11% YoY to ₹51,839 crore, driven primarily by 
volume growth across key markets. Contribution increased 17% to ₹21,338 crore, outpacing revenue growth due 
to favourable product mix, operational efficiencies and 
improved portfolio quality.
Contribution margins expanded by 220 basis points, 
while EBITDA increased 18% to ₹9,588 crore. This 
margin expansion reflects structural improvements in 
the business, supported by pricing discipline, product 
innovation, cost optimisation and portfolio management.
Our performance was broad-based, with PBT nearly 
fourfold versus LY, driven by strong EBITDA growth, lower 
finance costs and improved operating performance. 
Reported PATMI more than doubled. Excluding the one-
time tax provision reversal in FY25, operational PATMI 
increased to more than 2.5 times, illustrating a significant 
improvement in underlying profitability.
The consistent improvement across all line items in 
the income statement highlights the increasing quality 
of our business and our ability to deliver sustainable, 
profitable growth.
Converting growth into cash
Cash generation remained a key priority during FY26. 
Strong operating performance, disciplined working capital 
management and prudent capital allocation enabled 
healthy cash flows while supporting strategic investments.Free Cash Flow to Equity stood at ₹3,226 crore. Capital 
expenditure of approximately $261 million remained 
in line with guidance and was directed towards 
strategic growth initiatives, technology platforms and 
manufacturing capabilities.
Importantly, we were able to fund these investments 
while improving leverage metrics and maintaining 
strong liquidity, demonstrating the strength of our cash 
generation capabilities.
Driving working capital excellence
Improving capital productivity has been a major priority 
over the past two years. Through tighter inventory 
management, stronger collections and enhanced 
operational discipline, we have significantly improved 
working capital efficiency. I am pleased to report that our 
working capital cycle remained efficient at around 57 days. 
Maintaining this performance while delivering double-digit 
revenue growth reflects strong inventory management, 
receivables discipline and supply chain planning. In an 
industry characterised by seasonality and extended credit 
cycles, efficient working capital management remains a 
critical driver of cash flow and resilience.
Our objective extends beyond debt 
reduction. We remain focused on 
building a resilient capital structure 
capable of supporting growth 
through varying economic cycles. 
Our net debt-to-EBITDA improved to 
~1.6x in FY26.
Strengthening the balance sheet
One of the significant achievements of FY26 was the 
continued strengthening of our balance sheet.
Gross debt declined from ~$3.1 billion in FY25 to ~$2.3 
billion, a reduction of nearly 26%. Net debt reduced from 
around $2.0 billion to $1.6 billion, a decline of nearly 20%.
During the year, we repaid $850 million through debt 
repayments and redemption of perpetual securities. A 
significant milestone was the redemption of the $400 
million perpetual bond at its first call date in May 2025, 
funded entirely through internal cash accruals. We also 
repaid approximately $500 million of debt while continuing 
to fund operational and capital expenditure requirements.
These actions have materially strengthened our financial 
position and enhanced financial flexibility.Building a resilient capital structure
Our objective extends beyond deleveraging to building a 
resilient capital structure that supports growth through 
varying market conditions.
Net debt-to-EBITDA improved from 2.1x in FY25 to around 
1.6x in FY26, while net debt-to-equity improved from 0.5x 
to 0.4x. Improved profitability and capital efficiency also 
helped nearly double return on equity during the year.
We further strengthened liquidity by securing a $300 
million committed revolving credit facility. In addition, we 
successfully refinanced and extended a $400 million loan 
originally due in September 2026 to March 2029, improving 
our maturity profile and financial flexibility.
These developments reflect the confidence of lenders and 
financial institutions in UPL’s strategy, business model and 
financial discipline. Today, our capital structure is stronger 
and better positioned to support future growth.
Focused on sustainable value creation
As we look ahead, our priorities remain clear. We continue 
to accelerate profitable growth by focusing on high-
value opportunities across products, portfolios and 
geographies. At the same time, we will drive greater 
efficiency through portfolio optimisation, product 
rationalisation and disciplined capital allocation.
This balanced approach will strengthen earnings quality, 
improve capital productivity and create sustainable value 
for all stakeholders.
The progress achieved during FY26 reinforces our 
confidence in the resilience of our business model. Our 
diversified portfolio, global footprint and innovation-led 
strategy position us well to navigate uncertainty while 
capturing future growth opportunities.
We remain committed to improving portfolio quality, 
strengthening earnings resilience and enhancing 
capital efficiency. 
I would like to thank our employees, customers, partners, 
lenders and shareholders for their continued trust and 
support. The progress achieved during FY26 reflects a 
collective effort across the organisation and I am confident 
in our ability to build on this momentum in the years ahead.
Warm regards,
Bikash Prasad
Group CFO

Waste management
We embrace a circular economy through sustainable operations and we have adopted low-impact procedures and 
resource-efficient technologies to minimise waste generation. Recognising that the manufacturing of agrochemical 
products inevitably produces waste that can be hazardous to both people and the environment, we place great emphasis 
on the safe handling, management and disposal of all forms of waste, whether hazardous or non-hazardous. As we 
advance through FY26, leveraging automated tracking and specialised mitigation protocols across our manufacturing 
sites ensures our disposal systems meet the highest global standards for community and environmental safety.

Water management
We ensure responsible water management, aiming to cultivate positive environmental and community impacts within 
our areas of operation. To this end, we have actively achieved more than 50% Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) system status 
across our manufacturing sites globally by implementing world-class effluent reuse and recycling systems.  We continue 
to integrate advanced technologies, including Scale-Ban mechanical water treatment, which recycles high-TDS effluents 
to reduce cooling tower freshwater demand and specialised Reverse Osmosis systems to optimise water use and 
minimise waste. Our focus remains on maximising efficiency, contributing meaningfully to water conservation efforts 
and promoting sustainability.

Global advocacy spotlight: the #AFarmerCan campaign at COP30
Ahead of the United Nations Climate Change  
Conference (COP30) in Belém, Brazil, UPL launched its 
premier global advocacy initiative: '#AFarmerCan - The 
hero you don't know you need'. This campaign positions 
farmers at the very centre of global climate change 
strategies by showcasing 20 curated case studies of 
real-world growers championing soil regeneration, water conservation and biodiversity protection. 
The high-impact activation featured an immersive 
360-degree marketing rollout across Brazil, including 
more than 1,000 branded taxis and 200 transit buses 
in Belém embedded with digital QR codes, connecting 
global consumers directly to the untold stories of 
agricultural climate heroes.

Launched by UPL in 2015, the Sarus Conservation Project 
aims to protect the iconic Sarus Crane population in 
Gujarat’s Kheda and Anand districts. Through active 
community engagement, the project has achieved 
notable success, resulting in increased nesting rates 
and the identification of new breeding sites. Partnering 
closely with local communities, 'Rural Sarus Protection 
Groups' were established to combat egg theft, nest 
destruction and poaching, driving highly effective 
conservation measures. By the FY26 census, a total of 
1,477 Sarus cranes were recorded, marking a remarkable 
195% increase from the initial baseline count of 500 birds 
in FY16. 
Additionally, UPL continues to advance its Vulture

district to protect the critically endangered vulture 
species. With seven of India’s nine vulture species 
residing in Gujarat, this initiative documents local 
populations, breeding habits and ongoing environmental 
threats. Working hand-in-hand with regional 
communities, UPL focuses on raising awareness, forming 
dedicated protection groups and enhancing local 
capacity to safeguard critical vulture habitats. Driven 
by these grassroots efforts, including the formation 
of Jatayu Mitras volunteer networks comprising local 
farmers and youth, the project safeguards vital habitats 
and closely monitors regional vulture populations to

Global food security
As the global population reaches ~8.3 billion in 2026 and 
continues towards a potential 10.3 billion by 2084, the 
strain on food systems is intensifying.# Global hunger 
levels have remained alarmingly high; an estimated 8.2% 
of the global population, faced hunger in 2024. Current 
projections indicate that over 600 million people worldwide 
could still be facing hunger in 2030, with Sub-Saharan 
Africa remaining a critical region of concern as it faces 
major tests from conflict and energy shocks.@
This growing insecurity is not just a rural issue. In recent 
years, while over one-third of adults in rural areas 
experienced moderate to severe food insecurity, the 
share in urban areas was approximately 25%, showing 
a narrowing gap. Additionally, cities face their own 
challenges, such as fast food proliferation, declining access 
to fresh produce, marginalisation of small-scale farmers 
and the erosion of natural ecosystems due to unchecked 
urban expansion. Together, these dynamics, compounded 
by a projected 11.8% average inflation rate in the combined regions of Middle East and Africa for 2026, underscore the 
urgent need for resilient, inclusive and sustainable food 
systems that can nourish both growing populations and 
future generations.^Management

Macro-economic overview
Measured global resilience
The global economy proved resilient in 2025, despite ongoing 
policy shifts and trade uncertainties, achieving a 3.4% 
expansion according to the International Monetary Fund 
(IMF). The global inflation also moderated to 4.1%, providing 
major central banks with the baseline policy justification to 
initiate initial interest rate cuts.
This recovery trajectory faced immediate headwinds from 
the military conflict in West Asia at the end of February 2026. 
The resulting closure of primary shipping lanes has triggered 
renewed supply chain vulnerabilities and upward pressure 
on international energy costs. Consequently, global growth is 
projected to decelerate slightly, while global headline inflation is forecasted to climb back to 4.4% before stabilising at 3.7% 
in 2027, a premium that sits structurally above pre-pandemic 
baselines. Accordingly, a 'higher-for-longer' monetary stance 
is expected by central banks to keep borrowing cost tight.
The resurgence of energy and commodity prices has caused 
US inflation to return to target more gradually than other 
developed economies, such as Euro Area and Japan. 
Due to continued macroeconomic volatility, the growth 
trajectories were disparate across regions. According to IMF, 
North America has shown resilience and a growth rate of 1.9% 
for 2025 before accelerating to a forecast of 2.2% for 2026, whereas Europe posted a modest growth rate of 1.6% in 2025 and is projected to decelerate slightly to 1.3% in 2026 due to 
structural headwinds and high energy costs.
Emerging markets present a varied picture: China is forecasted to grow at 4.4% for 2026, supported by policy bank lending 
despite weak domestic demand. As per the World Bank Group, India remains the fastest-growing major economy, with 
momentum projected at 6.6% for 2026. Key risks to this outlook include the conflict in West Asia, with deeper geopolitical 
fragmentation and trade tensions.
*International Monetary Fund (IMF).
#World Population Prospect 2024.
@UN Sustainable Development Goals.
^CEBR: World Economic League Table (WELT) 2026 Report.Global energy shocks and crop dynamic shifts
Energy commodity prices face a structurally higher cost 
floor, with overall energy indices expected to rise due to 
operational disruptions in West Asia. This volatile overhead 
has restricted the availability of vital oil and gas derivatives 
and critical chemical raw materials, while maritime shipping 
bottlenecks through the Strait of Hormuz continue to keep 
global food prices elevated.
Because synthetic nutrient synthesis is highly 
energy-intensive, the resulting fertiliser shortages have fundamentally reshaped on-farm economics.  
Simultaneously, tariff adjustments, shifting trade 
partnerships and evolving China-US soybean trade 
dynamics introduce further macroeconomic volatility. 
As growers adapt by moving away from high-input cost 
regimes, upward pressure on manufacturing and logistics 
costs has sparked a notable price reversal and recovery at 
the ex-factory level for several active ingredients.

1. West Asia conflict and supply  
chain disruptions
The crisis in West Asia has introduced severe logistical 
and raw material constraints across the global chemical 
sector. Navigational gridlocks through the Strait of 
Hormuz, where globally traded nitrogen fertilisers 
normally transit, have triggered critical bottlenecks in 
procuring essential upstream intermediaries. These 
blockages forced major manufacturing hubs to heavily 
curtail or completely cease operations.
Simultaneously, severe container deficits have 
disrupted outbound shipping from East Asia due to 
prolonged transit delays within the conflict zone. 
During this period, geographically diversified 
companies carrying strategic safety stocks successfully 
protected customer delivery lines, temporarily passing 
input cost increases onto end-products.
Crucially, this disruption has established a higher 
baseline cost floor for raw chemical components. The 
average ex-factory spot prices for key products spiked 
sharply in March 2026, to reach their highest level since 
September 2023.2. Tariffs and supply chain bifurcation
Evolving trade regimes have fundamentally re-routed 
global agrochemical channels, driving a structural 
diversification of input sourcing away from China to 
ensure supply security. In North America, a peak 55% 
tariff on Chinese formulations historically created 
a steep tax differential against Indian alternatives. 
Concurrently, retaliatory tariffs redirected Chinese 
soybean demand away from the US towards 
Brazil and Argentina, expanding South American 
broadacre acreage and boosting regional crop 
protection volumes. 
While the recent February 2026 adjustment restored 
a 25% tariff advantage for Indian imports, ongoing 
volatility in applied tariffs continues to accelerate 
this supply chain shift. Indian chemical operations 
are uniquely positioned to capture this demand 
and are expected to gain an even wider commercial 
tariff advantage on specific reciprocal-exempt 
technical-grade materials, provided final blending and 
formulation occur domestically within the US market.
Indian economy
India’s economy demonstrated exceptional resilience, 
achieving a growth rate of 7.7% in FY26. Private Final 
Consumption Expenditure (PFCE) reached a decade-
high 61.5% of GDP, growing by 7% supported by robust 
domestic demand, income tax and GST reforms. Retail 
inflation remained well-contained at 3.5% as of April 2026, 
below the central bank's 4% medium-term target despite 
global energy price volatility.* 
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) shifted its policy stance 
from 'accommodative' to 'neutral' after cumulative repo 
rate cuts throughout 2025 bringing the key lending rate 
down to 5.25% in December.# Fiscal consolidation remains a priority, with the central 
government achieving a deficit of 4.8% in FY25 and 
targeting a further reduction to 4.4% for FY26. India 
continues to strengthen its position as a global supply 
chain alternative. In the chemicals sector, firms are 
leveraging a competitive cost base and domestic demand 
to build global-scale platforms, though continued 
investment in differentiated R&D and infrastructure 
remains critical for long-term dominance. 
Enduring strength of India’s agricultural sector
India stands tall as a significant contributor to the 
global agricultural sector, with approximately 43% of its 
population relying on it as a primary source of livelihood 
in 2025.* The country maintains its global leadership with 
the world’s largest areas under wheat, rice and cotton 
cultivation, while remaining the top producer of milk, 
pulses and spices. The sector is well-poised for growth, 
steadily enhancing its footprint in global food trade, with 
agricultural exports now exceeding $50 billion annually. 
According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, the agriculture 
sector has displayed resilience, registering a growth 
rate of 4.6% in FY26. This momentum reflects the impact 
of sustained government efforts to boost productivity, encourage high-value horticulture, which now accounts 
for a third of agricultural GVA and enhance farmer incomes 
through digital marketplaces like e-NAM. Agriculture 
remains a cornerstone of inclusive and sustainable 
economic progress toward the vision of Viksit Bharat.
For the upcoming Kharif season, crops such as paddy, 
pulses (tur and moong) and oilseeds (soybean and 
groundnut), provide an immediate volume pull for targeted 
crop protection inputs. However, this momentum may 
partially be countered by area contractions in maize and 
sugarcane due to shifting farmer choice and relative 
crop economics.
*Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).   #Reserve Bank of India (RBI).The El Niño factor: A polarised outlook for global agriculture
While El Niño weather pattern brings difficult conditions to farming hubs in SE Asia, India and North America, it 
drives strong harvest recovery across some parts of South America but with uneven impact - Argentina benefits 
from improved rainfall, while Brazil faces highly variable conditions. Historical evidence suggests El Niño years 
are generally less favourable for global agricultural output than neutral or La Niña years, with key staples such as 
maize, rice and wheat experiencing yield reductions across regions. 
Beyond direct yield impacts, this highlights the growing importance of crop protection and climate resilience 
technologies. Variable weather conditions contribute to elevated pest, weed and disease pressure in several 
markets, reinforcing demand for advanced crop protection solutions and resilient seed technologies aimed at 
helping growers manage increasingly volatile production environment. 
The increasing frequency and intensity of extreme weather events are expected to heighten the need 
for agricultural innovations that enhance crop resilience, protect yields and support global food security. 
Technologies that improve productivity while enabling sustainable use of resources will become increasingly 
critical to the long-term resilience of global food systems.

Industry overview
Transition continues as volumes recover and prices stabilise
The global crop protection volumes are improving as 
channel de-stocking nears completion. However, pricing 
pressure persists, particularly in herbicides driven by 
subdued farm economics, intense competition and 
continued oversupply from China. Against this backdrop, 
innovation in formulation, strong grower relationships and 
integrated solutions offerings remain key differentiators. 
Companies with differentiated portfolios, biological 
solutions and premium seed genetics and traits will 
continue to demonstrate stronger pricing power.
Global pricing is set to reflect higher raw material costs, 
potentially increasing input prices for growers. This may 
lead to shifts between molecules driving commercial 
rebalancing across portfolios as growers optimise 
spending to preserve margins.
The grower market for agrochemicals globally was valued 
at ~$78 billion* (including biocontrols) in 2025, calculated 
at ex-manufacturer prices. The market continues its steady 
recovery with an initial projected baseline expansion in 
low-single digit, influenced by a price impact and a modest 
volume increase, demonstrating resilience as supply chains 
become increasingly synchronised with real-time on-
farm consumption.
Importantly, the deflationary cycle for key generics appears 
to be moderating, supported by higher energy costs, raw-
material inflation, tighter Chinese export economics and 
China's reintroduction of export VAT on select molecules. 
However, manufacturers remain cautious: near-term 
outlook assumes minimal pricing recovery despite these 
early signs of stabilisation and profitability in the second 
half of 2026 is widely seen as dependent on successful 
price pass-through.A resilient volume base, moderating deflationary cycle and 
continued innovation and cost discipline point to gradual 
price normalisation through 2026, with the industry 
increasingly pivoting towards differentiated formulations, 
biologicals and specialty solutions. The principal swing 
factors remain the pace of price pass-through and the 
trajectory of energy and input costs tied to West Asia crisis, 
the interplay of which will determine the profitability for 
the year.

from volume to managed supply
The implementation of aggressive regulatory and 
fiscal reforms in China has established a price 
stabilisation signal for the global crop protection 
industry, bringing an end to three years of intense 
pricing-led margin compression driven by massive 
oversupply. This policy pivot is structurally raising 
the cost floor for Chinese exporters through a 
combination of strict anti-involution measures and 
the removal of export tax rebates on a broad range 
of chemical sets. This fiscal pressure is further 
reinforced by the January 2026 'one product, 
one certificate' registration regime, alongside 
strict 2026–2030 restrictions on greenfield 
petrochemical capacity permits as the country 
moves toward its post-2030 carbon peaking 
targets. Active ingredient prices are finding an 
overall reliable baseline that supports a gradual, 
long-awaited market value recovery through 2026.
*Crop protection market becomes $83 billion with conventional and biological products.  #AgbioInvestor.Biologicals growing fast but remain a niche sector
The biologicals industry continued to demonstrate resilience in 2025 despite ongoing headwinds supported by 
improved weather conditions, expanded crop plantings in key markets and increasing government focus on food 
security, sustainability and input-use efficiency. Global biologicals growth is estimated to have accelerated to the 
mid-to-high single digits, with Brazil remaining a key growth engine, supported by expanding soybean and maize 
acreage, the implementation of the Bioinputs Law and policy measures promoting greater adoption of biological 
inputs. In Europe, regulatory reforms aimed at simplifying and accelerating biocontrol approvals are expected to 
improve market access, while the gradual loss of conventional chemistries continues to support biological adoption. 
India remains a structurally attractive growth market, driven by favourable crop production trends, sustainability 
initiatives and increasing adoption of precision agriculture, despite short-term regulatory transition challenges. 
In North America, elevated fertiliser costs are strengthening demand for biostimulants focused on nutrient-use 
efficiency, reinforcing the sector’s role in improving farm productivity and sustainability.
Slowly entering mainstream; decadal play/opportunity
• Broadacre adoption:  Driven by proven field efficacy and climate pressures are rapidly expanding beyond 
specialty horticulture into major broadacre row crops.
• Regulatory tailwinds:  Market access is accelerating globally, led by Brazil and Europe, mainly as insecticides, 
exit the market, supporting an increasing pace of biological product introductions. At the same time, climate 
change is accelerating adoption of sustainable cultivation practices, further reinforcing shift towards biologicals 
and next-generation crop protection solutions.
• R&D frontiers:  Key innovation areas include nitrogen-fixing microbials, pheromones, peptide actives, 
RNAi formulation and artificial intelligence led natural-product discovery, alongside an increasing focus on 
bionematicides, plant extracts and advanced seed treatments.
• Strategic growth:  Long-term growth in conventional products will be eclipsed by strong gains in biologicals. 
At the same time, declining soil health in several regions and volatile chemical fertiliser prices are accelerating 
demand for nutrient-use efficiency solutions. Providers offering seamlessly integrated conventional and 
biological portfolios along with nutrient-use efficiency products are best positioned for this opportunity.
• M&A consolidation:  Global majors aggressively acquiring biological companies to secure established assets 
and fast-track portfolio diversification.

The global crop protection market is undergoing a 
structural shift, with post-patent molecules share 
at 84% of total market value. New active ingredient 
development has become increasingly expensive, 
costing over ~$350 million, nearly double the mid-
1990s levels, while development timelines have eased 
to about 11.4 years (2020-23) from a peak of ~12 years. 
The shift away from proprietary chemistries has been 
accelerated by a shrinking discovery pipeline among 
traditional R&D majors and rising innovator overheads, 
with complex registration processes for a single new 
molecule taking up to five years in markets. This innovation lag has opened a strong growth runway 
for the post-patent ecosystem, especially with a major 
wave of molecules expected to roll off-patent between 
2026-31. The transition creates a multibillion-dollar 
opportunity for cost competitive manufacturers to 
capture large volume channels across LATAM, Asia 
Pacific and Africa.
Consequently, the target addressable market for post-
patent, biological and integrated players is expected 
to grow a notch above the overall growth of the crop 
protection market over the next 5 years.POST-PATENT EXPANSION RUNWAY

Crop protection across key markets
The global crop protection market is navigating a complex 
landscape of recovery and volatility in 2025 and 2026. 
Following the significant destocking and pricing pressures 
of 2024, the current environment is bolstered by stabilising 
agrochemical prices and more synchronised inventory 
levels across the value chain. 
In 2025, the grower end-market for Europe showed 
growth, supported by biologicals uptake and favourable 
cropping, along with LATAM, while Asia Pacific declined. 
For MNCs, NAM was positively led by branded herbicide 
volumes, biologicals and new active ingredients benefiting 
from completed channel destocking.
In North America, the agricultural sector remains under 
pressure from subdued commodity prices and high 
production costs and a weak farm economy with USDA 
forecasting continued pressure on US crop input spending.
In Central and South America, market dynamics are heavily 
influenced by Brazil’s record soybean expansion and a 
notable recovery in Argentina, where favourable weather 
and a return to normal crop areas are supporting robust 
demand for herbicides and insecticides.* However, a weak 
farm economy in Brazil and high borrowing costs constrain 
farmer credit. Europe's market, while still managing 
erratic weather and the withdrawal of older chemistries, 
is seeing a return to growth supported by stable pricing 
and the rollout of next-generation fungicides and selective 
herbicides. The Asia Pacific region, is driving adoption of 
novel modes of action to tackle resistant pest populations.Global seeds market to return to growth in 2026
While the crop protection segment signals continued 
recovery in 2026, the global seed market continues 
to navigate complex headwinds driven by fluctuating 
farm fundamentals and a highly differentiated regional 
landscape. In APAC, maize, rapeseed, soybean and 
vegetables indicate growth, but rice oversupply remains a 
concern for value development. In Argentina, the country’s 
maize and sunflower sectors are expected to grow with 
~24% and 33% larger areas, respectively. Conversely, the 
market remains tempered by challenging agri-economics 
in North America, where maize acreage is projected to fall 
in the current cycle.
On a regional level, North America is expected to fall while 
all other regions rebound. This represents a complete 
structural reversal from the previous cycle; the traded seed 
market had contracted by an estimated 2.1% to roughly $47.5 
billion, dragged down severely by Central & South America 
and Europe (low-single digit decline), a period during which 
North America was the only region to experience low-single 
digit growth. The global traded seed market is projected to 
demonstrate resilience, with a long-term growth forecast 
averaging ~1% annually through 2030.*

Evolving dynamics in crop protection strategies
The landscape of crop protection in FY26 is undergoing a 
structural transformation, with the global market projected 
to expand at a CAGR of ~2% over the next five years. In Brazil 
and Argentina, the rising adoption of insect-resistant crop 
varieties is structurally reducing reliance on traditional 
insecticides,  though periodic outbreaks of resistant and 
secondary pests continue to support demand for targeted 
insecticide applications in both markets. 
The industry is also witnessing a shift toward precision and 
digital agriculture. The industry is increasingly adopting 
precision agriculture technologies, including AI-enabled 
targeted spraying and variable-rate application tools, 
which can significantly reduce input use and application 
waste. At the same time, value creation is increasingly 
shifting toward higher-performance proprietary active 
ingredients and advanced formulation technologies that 
deliver greater efficacy, mix compatibility and sustainability 
benefits, commanding higher margins. The complexities are 
compounded by strict regulatory mandates, such as the EU's 
permanent ban on neonicotinoid seed treatments, which in 
2026 is leaving critical gaps in pest control and driving the 
search for high-value alternatives like spinosad or diamide-
based programmes to safeguard crop yields.Long-term structural global drivers and disruptors

India’s crop protection market
India, the world’s fourth-largest producer of crop 
protection chemicals, continues to play a pivotal role in 
global agriculture by strengthening its foreign exchange 
reserves as a net exporter. In FY26, India’s crop protection 
market (including exports) is valued at an impressive  
₹695 billion, accounting for roughly 13% of the global 
industry.* As the global spotlight intensifies on sustainable 
food production, the importance of India’s crop protection 
sector is only growing. In the face of mounting pressure 
to produce more with fewer resources, Indian companies 
have not only helped farmers enhance crop yields and 
reduce losses but have also positioned the country as a 
major exporter in this critical industry. Their contribution 
is especially relevant as the world transitions towards 
regenerative farming practices aimed at preserving 
environmental health while boosting productivity.
However, emerging trends such as population growth, 
digital transformation and the rise of direct-to-farmer 
models, including sales through Farmer Producer 
Organisations (FPOs) and e-commerce platforms, are 
helping bridge this gap and redefine market dynamics. In 
FY26, the domestic market is estimated to have contributed 46%, while exports lead the way with a commanding 
54% share. The sector is gradually increasing the share 
of differentiated and premium offerings while generics 
continue to account for the majority of industry volumes.
This domestic shift towards high-value portfolios occurs 
alongside complex local input stresses. Driven by West Asia 
supply anxieties, channel replenishment and pre-Kharif 
stocking supported demand ahead of the season, fuelled 
by high demand for affordable post-patent chemistries. 
This buying surge is further complicated by severe 
international pricing pressure. While global urea prices 
softened, domestic non-urea nutrient costs escalated, 
forcing the Government of India to increase subsidy outlays 
to protect grower economics.

and spray windows

resurgence in demand after a decline in preceding years, 
spurred by satisfactory reservoir levels (at 127% of normal) 
that bolstered volume growth. Domestic revenues rose

UPL is a leading global provider of sustainable agricultural 
products and solutions, serving growers in more than 
140 countries with an annual revenue of $6 billion. The 
Company operates on an agile, 'pure-play' platform model 
designed to drive innovation, capital discipline and food 
security across the entire agrifood value chain. Recognised 
globally for its environmental, social and governance 
leadership, UPL holds the top sustainability ranking in its 
sector, pioneering climate-smart initiatives like agricultural 
carbon credit programmes and biological footprint 
expansion on the world stage. 
The Company’s operations are divided into four distinct 
business segments tailored to specific agricultural and chemical markets: UPL Corporation handles the 
international crop protection business, focusing on high-
value differentiated and natural biological solutions; UPL 
SAS drives the domestic crop protection and robust brand 
portfolios specifically for the Indian market; Advanta 
Enterprises operates as a global seed powerhouse 
specialising in climate-resilient hybrids, newly scaling its 
reach through the strategic integration of DECCO post-
harvest technologies; and SUPERFORM Chemistries serves 
as the group's highly competitive specialty chemical 
manufacturing arm, rapidly scaling contract manufacturing 
across pharmaceutical, mining and industrial sectors.
The connected field: Driving innovation at the intersection of seeds, biologicals and data
The future of agricultural crop science belongs to 
platforms that can seamlessly combine elite plant 
genetics, natural biological inputs and real-time 
digital field intelligence into a single, cohesive user 
experience. By linking our high-performing Advanta 
seed varieties with our Natural Plant Protection 
(NPP) portfolio and direct-to-grower digital tools like 
nurture.farm, we have unlocked an incredibly asset-
light path to market leadership. This unified system 
acts through three distinct engines: Advanta channels 
significant investment of its top-line revenue into R&D to build climate-smart, non-GM hybrids that naturally 
withstand extreme heat and drought stress; our 
biological division deploys residue-free, eco-friendly 
inputs like Nuvita® to revitalise soil health; and our 
data applications provide precision advisory alerts that 
help growers defeat labour shortages and optimise 
field applications by successfully bridging the historic 
gap between seeds and crop chemistry, UPL delivers 
superior, climate-resilient crop yields for growers while 
fundamentally insulating our corporate margins and 
upgrading our premium product mix.

A key highlight this year is that every structural component 
of our cash flow has improved over the previous year. 
EBITDA ± non-cash items rose by more than ` 2,000 crore, 
while interest costs, tax costs, and other balance sheet 
items such as non-current and current assets all reduced 
meaningfully. Across the Board, each element of the cash 
flow has delivered stronger than last year.Given the seasonal nature of our business, cash flow is best 
assessed on a working capital-adjusted basis. The working 
capital cycle currently stands at around 57 days. Typically, 
the cycle lengthens through Q1 and Q2 as net debt builds, 
remains largely flat in Q3, and sees a significant release in 
Q4, when close to a billion dollars of cash flow is freed up 
each year. Viewed on this adjusted basis, the underlying 
cash generation of the business is robust.
Risk management
Risk management is a fundamental base of UPL’s 
strategic planning and decision-making. The business 
takes a preventive stance in detecting, assessing and 
reducing risks that might obstruct the attainment of its 
targets. This method safeguards its holdings, maintains 
its standing, guarantees legal adherence and supports 
stakeholder belief. 
The Company’s Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) 
structure is supported by explicitly assigned tasks, governing values, uniform equipment and extensive 
schooling. Synced with globally accepted protocols like ISO 
31000 and COSO, the firm’s strong ERM process advances 
a climate of autonomy, prediction and uniformity in risk 
management. By integrating this structure throughout the 
entity, UPL is fully prepared to handle existing and future 
threats, while grabbing strategic possibilities to foster 
long-term wealth and stability.
We delivered across all three pillars of our financial strategy, balancing our volume-driven revenue growth of 11% with

OPERATIONAL PERFORMANCE 
During the period under review, the Company delivered a strong 
and resilient performance, achieving consolidated revenue of 
₹51,839 crore, reflecting a growth of 11% over the previous 
year, primarily driven by higher volumes and favourable foreign exchange movements. EBITDA grew by 18% to ₹9,588 crore, 
supported by improved contribution margins on account 
of enhanced capacity utilisation and lower input costs. The 
Company reported a significant improvement in profitability, with Profit Before Tax increasing nearly fourfold and operational 
PAT growing by more than 2.7 times year-on-year, demonstrating 
strong operational efficiency and disciplined cost management. 
The balance sheet was further strengthened through effective 
capital management, with a reduction in gross debt by ₹5,078 
crore, and improvement in leverage metrics, with net debt to 
EBITDA at ~1.6 times as at the end of the year. 
The aforesaid performance underscores the Company’s ability 
to deliver better results despite a challenging macroeconomic 
environment impacting the global agricultural sector. 
RIGHTS ISSUE 
During the year, the Rights Issue Committee approved the 
issuance of Second and Final Call notice on the partly paid-up 
Rights Equity Shares.
Accordingly, the Company issued the Call Notice to the eligible 
shareholders for balance payment of ₹180 per partly paid-up 
equity share. The Company received an aggregate amount 
of ₹1,671.79 crore on 9,27,15,506 equity shares, representing 
approximately 99% of the total amount due on the Second and 
Final Call. 
Subsequently, the Rights Issue Committee, approved the 
issuance of a Final Reminder-cum-Forfeiture Notice to those 
holders of partly paid-up equity shares who had failed to pay the 
First Call, and/or Second and Final Call, or both. After issuance 
of the final reminder cum forfeiture notice, 15,859 shareholders 
holding 8,46,171 partly paid up equity shares paid the pending 
call money and were subsequently converted into fully paid up 
equity shares. 2,64,278 Rights Equity Shares, held by 10,733 
shareholders, were forfeited as per the provisions of Articles of 
Association of the Company and in accordance with the Letter of 
Offer dated November 20, 2024 due to non-receipt of call money 
within the stipulated time. 
Consequent to the above actions, 9,35,61,677 partly paid-up 
equity shares became fully paid up.
